zebralogic.title: Preserve exact case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: Output attribute values using the same spelling and case as listed in the problem; any deviation (e.g., capitalizing a color) will cause a mismatch with the expected answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When generating the final JSON answer for a zebra‑logic puzzle.
zebralogic.example: Writing "Green" instead of "green" for a color attribute.

zebralogic.title: Direct adjacency (directly left of)
zebralogic.principle: Treat "X is directly left of Y" as X's house = Y's house - 1, preserving left‑right orientation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing clues that specify "directly left of".
zebralogic.example: Placing X two houses left of Y because the clue was misread as "somewhere left of".

zebralogic.title: Relative ordering (somewhere left of)
zebralogic.principle: Treat "X is somewhere to the left of Y" as X's house < Y's house, without requiring adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing clues that use "somewhere to the left/right of".
zebralogic.example: Assuming X must be immediately left of Y, placing them adjacent when they could be farther apart.

zebralogic.title: Adjacency without orientation (next to each other)
zebralogic.principle: Interpret "X and Y are next to each other" as |X - Y| = 1, with no implied left/right order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says two items are next to each other.
zebralogic.example: Fixing X left of Y when the clue only says they are adjacent.

zebralogic.title: Exact distance (houses between)
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says "There are N houses between X and Y", enforce |X - Y| = N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing clues that specify a number of houses between two items.
zebralogic.example: Treating "two houses between" as distance 2 instead of 3.

zebralogic.title: Combine consecutive adjacency constraints into a block
zebralogic.principle: If clues create a chain like A left of B and B left of C, treat A‑B‑C as three consecutive houses in that order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When multiple adjacency clues involve overlapping items.
zebralogic.example: Placing volleyball, baseball, brown hair in non‑consecutive houses despite clues linking them consecutively.

zebralogic.title: Equivalence linking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states "X is the same as Y" (e.g., "the person with red hair is the person who loves white"), assign both attributes to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing clues that equate two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Assigning red hair to a different house than the white color.

zebralogic.title: Fixed house assignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house (e.g., "the person who loves white is in the fifth house"), place that attribute in that house immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue gives an absolute house number.
zebralogic.example: Leaving the white color unassigned to house 5 despite the clue.

zebralogic.title: Exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: Respect clues that forbid an attribute from a specific house (e.g., "the person who loves tennis is not in the fifth house") by eliminating that house from consideration.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains "not in" or similar negation.
zebralogic.example: Placing tennis in house 5 despite the restriction.

zebralogic.title: Multi‑attribute equivalence
zebralogic.principle: When a clue links several attributes together (e.g., "the person who has auburn hair is the person who loves the stew"), assign all linked attributes to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue ties two or more attributes to the same person.
zebralogic.example: Assigning auburn hair to a house with a different food.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model defaults to title case when generating text, forgetting that the puzzle expects the exact case used in the problem statement.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute values verbatim from the problem description, preserving lower case (or the exact case shown).

zebralogic.description: Capitalization mismatch for phone model values
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Brand names are treated as proper nouns and are automatically capitalized, which differs from the lower‑case strings given in the puzzle.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Refer to the exact spelling of phone model strings as listed in the problem (usually all lower case) and output them unchanged.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may stop after satisfying a subset of clues, especially when the clue set is large and complex, leading to an apparently plausible but invalid grid.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After constructing a candidate solution, systematically verify every clue; if any clue is unsatisfied, backtrack and adjust the assignments.
